question: GQ-001
subject: I killed my own rebuild 40 minutes in
what_i_did: started a 200-book fetch while a rebuild was running, reasoning that the remaining stages only READ the index
why_that_was_wrong: the modern-spelling build holds a long WRITE transaction over 2.59M rows, and the ingester writes to the same database
the_failure: Runtime error near line 1: database is locked (5) — step 3 died, 40 minutes of indexing wasted
cost_was_time_not_data: the passage index had already completed: 1,725 books, 2,593,708 passages intact
the_asymmetry_that_hid_it: --check already detects an in-flight fetch by watching the text count move; the REBUILD path never did — and the rebuild path is the half that actually loses work
the_fix: refuse_if_ingesting at start AND immediately before step 3, since the failure case was an ingest started AFTER the rebuild began
a_second_slip_i_caught: ps aux | grep -c counted its own pipeline and told me an ingest was still running when none was; confirmed by checking the log had stopped growing
